## Background

Scenario: `batch.facLoc0.3_de.facLoc0.1_nbatch4_ngroup4_groupCells1000`
(4 batches, 4 cell-type groups, moderate batch effect, moderate DE signal).
Four perturbation axes, each compared back to the unperturbed baseline:

1. **LOGO** (leave-one-group-out) -- drop each of the 4 groups, one at a time.
2. **LOBO** (leave-one-batch-out) -- drop each of the 4 batches, one at a time.
3. **Sparsity** -- a fresh simulation at the same parameters with
   `dropout.mid=3.5` (~88% zero entries, vs. ~32% for the baseline).
4. **Composition skew** -- unlike LOGO, all 4 groups stay present, just
   reweighted: (a) `skewed10_20_30_40` (Group1-4 = 10/20/30/40%) and (b)
   `rareGroup1_1pct` (Group1 = 1%, Groups 2-4 = 33% each). Same per-batch
   cell budget as the baseline, so only the proportions differ.

Datasets generated by `scripts/notebooks/simulate_mixed_effects.Rmd`. Gene
selection, integration, and metrics come from the Snakemake pipeline run
with `scripts/config_files/config_mixed_effects.yml`. The full pairwise
anglemania z-score tables (not just the top-n_genes list) come from
`scripts/python/stability_anglemania_stats.py`. All combined and summarised by
`scripts/R/stability_analyse_mixed_effects.R`.

A separate sanity check (`scripts/R/sanity_check_r_vs_pyanglemania.R`) compares
pyanglemania against the original R `anglemania` implementation on 2 of
these samples (baseline and `dropGroupGroup1`), to rule out a Python-port
bug as the explanation for the instability seen below.

```{r libraries}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggbeeswarm)
library(ggrepel)

theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11))
method_colors <- c(angl = "#4393C3", hvg = "#D6604D")
perturbation_colors <- c(logo = "#4DAF4A", lobo = "#377EB8", sparsity = "#E41A1C", composition = "#984EA3")
```

```{r paths}
MIXED_EFFECTS_DIR <- "/local/Projects/AAkalin_Neuroblastoma/Results/simulate_single_cell/h5ad/mixed_effects"
STABILITY_DIR <- file.path(MIXED_EFFECTS_DIR, "pipeline_output", "stability")
```

## Load results

```{r load}
gene_set_stability <- read_tsv(file.path(STABILITY_DIR, "gene_set_stability.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
zscore_stability    <- read_tsv(file.path(STABILITY_DIR, "zscore_stability.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
metrics_deltas      <- read_tsv(file.path(STABILITY_DIR, "metrics_deltas.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

pert_levels <- c("logo", "lobo", "sparsity", "composition")
gene_set_stability$perturbation_type <- factor(gene_set_stability$perturbation_type, levels = pert_levels)
zscore_stability$perturbation_type   <- factor(zscore_stability$perturbation_type, levels = pert_levels)
metrics_deltas$perturbation_type     <- factor(metrics_deltas$perturbation_type, levels = pert_levels)

gene_set_stability
```

---

## Experiment: Gene-set stability (Jaccard / RBO) vs baseline

```{r geneset-plot}
ggplot(gene_set_stability, aes(x = perturbation_type, y = jaccard, fill = gene_selection)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 1, position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
  ggbeeswarm::geom_beeswarm(dodge.width = 0.8, size = 1.5, alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = method_colors) +
  labs(title = "Jaccard(baseline, perturbed) top-n_genes gene set",
       subtitle = "Higher = more reproducible gene set under this perturbation",
       x = "Perturbation type", y = "Jaccard")

ggplot(gene_set_stability, aes(x = perturbation_type, y = rbo_score, fill = gene_selection)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 1, position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
  ggbeeswarm::geom_beeswarm(dodge.width = 0.8, size = 1.5, alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = method_colors) +
  labs(title = "Rank-biased overlap(baseline, perturbed)",
       subtitle = "Higher = more reproducible ranking, weighted toward top of list",
       x = "Perturbation type", y = "RBO")
```

```{r geneset-detail, fig.height=5}
ggplot(gene_set_stability, aes(x = reorder(perturbation_detail, influence), y = influence, fill = gene_selection)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge()) +
  facet_wrap(~perturbation_type, scales = "free_x") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = method_colors) +
  labs(title = "Influence (1 - Jaccard) per dropped group / batch / sparsity level",
       x = NULL, y = "Influence")
```

## Experiment: anglemania mean_zscore stability on shared gene pairs

```{r zscore-plot}
ggplot(zscore_stability, aes(x = perturbation_type, y = spearman_r)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 1, fill = method_colors["angl"]) +
  ggbeeswarm::geom_beeswarm(size = 1.5, alpha = 0.6) +
  labs(title = "Spearman correlation of mean_zscore on shared gene pairs (baseline vs perturbed)",
       subtitle = "Lower = z-scores reshuffle more under this perturbation, even for pairs present in both",
       x = "Perturbation type", y = "Spearman r")

ggplot(zscore_stability, aes(x = reorder(perturbation_detail, spearman_r), y = spearman_r)) +
  geom_col(fill = method_colors["angl"]) +
  facet_wrap(~perturbation_type, scales = "free_x") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Per-perturbation mean_zscore Spearman correlation vs baseline",
       x = NULL, y = "Spearman r")
```

```{r zscore-npairs}
zscore_stability %>% select(sample_name, perturbation_type, perturbation_detail, n_shared_pairs, pearson_r, spearman_r)
```

## Worked example: 100 genes, ~2000-5000 pairs

The aggregate correlations above are computed over the full 9-17M gene-pair
table per sample. To make that concrete, this section tracks a fixed,
legible example: the **100 genes anglemania ranks most confidently on the
baseline** (lowest gene-pair rank, i.e. the "core" of the selection), and
every pairwise `mean_zscore` among them (up to 100*99/2 = 4950 pairs; fewer
are shown per sample because anglemania's own prefilter threshold drops some
pairs before ranking -- see `scripts/R/stability_gene_subset_example.R`).

```{r gene-subset-load}
gene_subset_zscores <- read_tsv(file.path(STABILITY_DIR, "gene_subset_example_zscores.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
gene_subset_summary <- read_tsv(file.path(STABILITY_DIR, "gene_subset_example_summary.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
gene_subset_genes   <- read_tsv(file.path(STABILITY_DIR, "gene_subset_example_genes.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

gene_subset_summary$perturbation_type <- factor(gene_subset_summary$perturbation_type, levels = pert_levels)
gene_order <- gene_subset_genes$gene

gene_subset_summary %>% arrange(perturbation_type, mean_abs_delta)
```

```{r gene-subset-summary-plot, fig.height=5}
ggplot(gene_subset_summary, aes(x = reorder(perturbation_detail, mean_abs_delta), y = mean_abs_delta, fill = perturbation_type)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~perturbation_type, scales = "free_y") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = perturbation_colors, guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Mean |z-score delta| vs baseline, within the 100-gene example subset",
       x = NULL, y = "Mean absolute mean_zscore delta")

ggplot(gene_subset_summary, aes(x = reorder(perturbation_detail, pearson_r), y = pearson_r, fill = perturbation_type)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~perturbation_type, scales = "free_y") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = perturbation_colors, guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Pearson correlation of mean_zscore vs baseline, within the 100-gene example subset",
       subtitle = "This core subset stays far more correlated than the full aggregate reported above --\nthe instability is concentrated in genes/pairs *outside* this confidently-ranked core",
       x = NULL, y = "Pearson r")
```

```{r gene-subset-scatter, fig.height=7}
baseline_zscores_subset <- gene_subset_zscores %>%
  filter(perturbation_type == "baseline") %>%
  select(pair_key, baseline_zscore = mean_zscore)

scatter_subset <- gene_subset_zscores %>%
  filter(perturbation_type != "baseline") %>%
  inner_join(baseline_zscores_subset, by = "pair_key")

ggplot(scatter_subset, aes(x = baseline_zscore, y = mean_zscore, color = perturbation_type)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.8, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  facet_wrap(~perturbation_detail, ncol = 4) +
  scale_color_manual(values = perturbation_colors, guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Baseline vs perturbed mean_zscore, 100-gene example subset",
       subtitle = "Each point is one gene pair among the 100 example genes; dashed line = no change",
       x = "Baseline mean_zscore", y = "Perturbed mean_zscore")
```

```{r gene-subset-heatmap-fn}
plot_zscore_heatmap <- function(sample, title) {
  df <- gene_subset_zscores %>% filter(sample_name == sample)
  df_sym <- bind_rows(
    df %>% select(geneA, geneB, mean_zscore),
    df %>% select(geneA = geneB, geneB = geneA, mean_zscore)
  ) %>%
    mutate(geneA = factor(geneA, levels = gene_order),
           geneB = factor(geneB, levels = gene_order))

  ggplot(df_sym, aes(x = geneA, y = geneB, fill = mean_zscore)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", midpoint = 0, na.value = "grey95") +
    theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank()) +
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "mean_zscore")
}

baseline_sample_name_lookup <- gene_subset_zscores %>% filter(perturbation_type == "baseline") %>% pull(sample_name) %>% unique()
lobo_batch1_sample <- gene_subset_zscores %>% filter(perturbation_type == "lobo", perturbation_detail == "Batch1") %>% pull(sample_name) %>% unique()
sparsity_sample <- gene_subset_zscores %>% filter(perturbation_type == "sparsity") %>% pull(sample_name) %>% unique()
```

```{r gene-subset-heatmap-plots, fig.height=6}
plot_zscore_heatmap(baseline_sample_name_lookup, "Baseline")
plot_zscore_heatmap(lobo_batch1_sample, "LOBO: Batch1 dropped (most stable axis, Pearson r = 0.99)")
plot_zscore_heatmap(sparsity_sample, "Sparsity: dropout.mid3.5, ~88% zero (least stable axis, Pearson r = 0.70)")
```

Genes/gene-order for these heatmaps (rows and columns both sorted by
baseline rank, so the top-left corner holds the most confidently-selected
pairs); grey tiles are pairs that didn't clear anglemania's prefilter
threshold in that particular sample.

## Experiment: Integration metric deltas vs baseline

```{r metrics-plot, fig.height=5}
metrics_long <- metrics_deltas %>%
  select(sample, perturbation_type, perturbation_detail, integration_method, gene_selection,
         `Bio conservation_delta`, `Batch correction_delta`, `Total_delta`) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = ends_with("_delta"), names_to = "score", values_to = "delta") %>%
  mutate(score = sub("_delta$", "", score))

ggplot(metrics_long, aes(x = perturbation_type, y = delta, fill = gene_selection)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 1, position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40") +
  facet_grid(score ~ integration_method) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = method_colors) +
  labs(title = "Integration score delta vs baseline (perturbed - baseline)",
       subtitle = "Below 0 = perturbation hurt this score relative to the unperturbed baseline",
       x = "Perturbation type", y = "Score delta")
```

```{r metrics-scatter, fig.height=5}
ggplot(metrics_deltas, aes(x = `Bio conservation_delta`, y = `Batch correction_delta`, color = gene_selection, shape = perturbation_type)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray70") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray70") +
  facet_wrap(~integration_method) +
  scale_color_manual(values = method_colors) +
  labs(title = "Bio conservation vs Batch correction delta, per perturbed sample",
       x = "Bio conservation delta", y = "Batch correction delta")
```

```{r metrics-table}
metrics_deltas %>% arrange(perturbation_type, integration_method, gene_selection)
```

## Sanity check: does pyanglemania mirror the original R anglemania?

The instability seen above is specific to anglemania's gene *selection*
criterion, not an artifact of the Python port: on the same data, R
`anglemania` and pyanglemania agree far more with each other than
pyanglemania agrees with itself across perturbations.

```{r r-vs-py}
r_vs_py <- read_tsv(file.path(STABILITY_DIR, "r_vs_pyanglemania_sanity_check.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
r_vs_py
```

```{r r-vs-py-plot, fig.height=4}
comparison_df <- bind_rows(
  r_vs_py %>% transmute(sample, jaccard, comparison = "R vs pyanglemania\n(same data)"),
  gene_set_stability %>% filter(gene_selection == "angl", perturbation_type %in% c("logo", "lobo")) %>%
    transmute(sample = sample_name, jaccard, comparison = "pyanglemania vs itself\n(LOGO/LOBO perturbed data)")
)

ggplot(comparison_df, aes(x = comparison, y = jaccard, fill = comparison)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 1, width = 0.5) +
  ggbeeswarm::geom_beeswarm(size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2", guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "R vs Python implementation agreement vs. pyanglemania's own perturbation instability",
       subtitle = "If the left box were much lower than the right, that would point to a porting bug -- it isn't",
       x = NULL, y = "Jaccard (top-2000 genes)")
```
